surfaces.part: shelf compartments with goods (upper and lower tiers)

answer.evidence: Rows 1-4 form a band that shifts from grayish pink to near-white. Row 5 is a white edge line, rows 6-7 are a pink edge, and rows 8-9 are a darker pink eave shadow. This is a weak top surface of about 5 rows. Below it, rows 10-27 show the open shelf front with goods, a divider at rows 18-19, and a dark base at rows 28-29. The front face is 3+ rows. There is no receding side face. The top reading is ambiguous because the band could also be a front-facing header or sign.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a pink and white shelf unit with small colored product dots. Measured facts: 21 visible tones per tile, matching prop-well-roofed (20) and prop-stall-cheese (17), 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted and not near-black. By eye the shelf is rather small and clean. The pink and white shading has about 4 steps against the reference's 5-6. The shelf bands are fairly uniform and the product dots are sparse. There is little grain or per-surface texture, and the body is mostly smooth stripes. The measured density holds up, but the structure and shading craft is a little simpler than the stall and well references. A careful artist might accept it, but it looks slightly flatter, so I'm failing it when in doubt.
